Schedule pilot kickoff (product + infra) for week of 2026-12-20

summary: Redwood demo focused on data handling and retention controls: request storage toggles, PII redaction in logs, logging redaction rules, KMS integration, audit logs, and privacy options for Dedicated/Private deployments. Customer concerned about PCI/PII scope and wanting clear retention toggles and proof-of-deletion for requests.

Audit logs and export for compliance
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private implications for data residency
transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-12-10 16:00 UTC  Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), Sara Gomez (Borealis), Tom Wu (Borealis), Priya Nair (Borealis)
---
00:00:03 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm maya with redwood, and with me is liam our se, we'll run through how our platform handles request storage, redaction, and retention toggles, and then we can jump into the console for a quick demo
00:00:20 Sara: thanks maya, quick context - we're a payments processor, lots of pci and pII surface, so main goal is minimizing data retained from requests and having auditable deletions, also want to understand dedicated vs hosted implications
00:00:35 Liam: totally, that's exactly what we'll show. quick agenda: overview of storage toggles -> demo of console toggles and api flags -> redaction rules -> kms integration and audit logs -> q&a and next steps
00:01:10 Priya: timeline wise we're aiming to decide vendor by end of q1, pilot needed earlier, and security needs the SOC2 and architecture docs
00:01:30 Tom: and i care about proof of deletion and whether logs still contain PII after you enable retention off, like do request bodies get fully purged or just marked?
00:01:50 Liam: good question, i'll show the difference - we have a per-organization default + per-route overrides. 'request_storage': "off" will prevent request bodies from being stored in our long-term store, short-term ephemeral caching may still exist for a handful of seconds for inference, but KV cache and telemetry are scrubbed if you enable redaction. we also provide a secure wipe operation recorded in audit logs.
00:02:30 Sara: when you say 'redaction' is that regex-based or more advanced? can we map fields like card_number or ssn?
00:02:50 Maya: both - we expose a rules engine in the console. basic regex scrub, json-path field suppression, and built-in pii detectors (they sometimes mis-tag, so you can tune). liam will demo the rules UI.
00:03:25 Liam: heading to the console now  opening Project -> Data Controls -> Request Storage.
00:03:58 [screen share starts - console slightly laggy]
00:04:10 Liam: here you see org-level toggle: 'Store requests' ON/OFF, retention window dropdown (7d, 30d, 90d, infinite). then per-route overrides beneath. i'll flip a demo route to OFF.
00:04:45 Tom: does 'OFF' truly prevent us from retrieving past requests? because auditors ask for retrieval sometimes, but we want minimal retention 
00:05:00 Liam: OFF means we do not persist request bodies to long-term object storage. metadata (non-PII request id, timestamp, model used) is retained for observability and billing unless you opt-in to minimal audit-only metadata, which we can discuss with legal. we log the deletion operation with a tamper-evident entry in audit logs (signed by our control plane key if in hosted; in Private you can configure your HSM).
00:05:40 Priya: key management - do you support customer-managed keys?
00:05:50 Liam: yes. KMS integrations: AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and we support HSM for Private. you can choose envelope encryption for stored items. also note: in Dedicated we can offer separate tenancy for key wrapping.
00:06:20 Sara: are there APIs for programmatic deletion? auditors want an API call and a proof-of-deletion response
00:06:35 Maya: yes, there's a 'delete-requests' endpoint that will return a job id and eventual status. we also generate a signed audit record (contains job id, timestamp, scope) accessible from Audit -> Exports. we'll include a sample in the security pack.
00:07:05 Tom: what about redaction accuracy? worried about false negatives, like an address in free text
00:07:20 Liam: built-in detectors use heuristics and token pattern matching; for high-assurance you can define explicit json-path filters for your API payloads, and we recommend instrumenting a small set of canonical fields to always be stripped. also we can run a sample pass with our 'Optimize' tool to suggest fields based on traffic.
00:08:00 Priya: can we run a POC with anonymized sample traffic first? not willing to share live customer data
00:08:10 Maya: absolutely. typical flow is: 1) run a sandbox with synthetic or scrubbed data 2) run a 48-72 hour retention test with sample traffic under 'store requests' toggled on to capture patterns, then flip to off and verify deletion 3) pilot if results good
00:08:40 [crosstalk]
00:09:00 Liam: demoing redaction rules page: create new rule -> name, match based on header or body -> regex or json-path -> action: redact or replace with token. watch: i'll add rule to redact card_number fields matching "^4[0-9]{12}(?:[0-9]{3})?$" as example. console shows preview of scrubbed sample.
00:10:05 Sara: preview looks good, but in logs we need to keep trace ids for debugging - will those be preserved?
00:10:20 Liam: yes, trace ids and minimal metadata can be preserved, but you can choose to hash trace ids if you want even less linkability. also we support tokenization where original sensitive values are replaced with hashed tokens stored encrypted with your CMK.
00:11:00 Tom: does hashing count as retaining PII under pci, because a reversible mapping could be considered sensitive
00:11:20 Maya: that's why we recommend one-way hashing or pseudonymization with rotating salts you control in customer-managed KMS. we can work with your compliance team on acceptable patterns.
00:12:00 Priya: show me the API flag you mentioned earlier for per-request control
00:12:15 Liam: sure  the API accepts header x-redwood-store-requests: true/false, and x-redwood-redaction-profile: <profile-id>. we'll paste sample curl.
00:12:40 [liam pastes curl sample in chat]
00:13:10 Sara: if a route gets high QPS, disabling request storage could impact debugging, right? do you have request-sampling?
00:13:25 Liam: yes we do adaptive sampling and an additional lightweight telemetry stream that captures anonymized metrics for SLOs. you can configure a sampling ratio per-route; also 'retention off but sample 0.1%' pattern is common.
00:14:00 Tom: audit logs  are they immutable and exportable?
00:14:10 Liam: audit logs are append-only; in Hosted they're stored with signatures and available for export to your SIEM via S3 or syslog. in Private you can fully control the storage location. exports are available as compressed signed bundles.
00:14:45 Sara: can we get a sample audit bundle?
00:14:55 Maya: yes we'll include a sanitized sample in the security docs.
00:15:10 [short pause while demo loads]
00:15:40 Liam: switching to retention lifecycle: you can set retention per-route and set auto-deletion windows; we have a 'ttl enforcement' job that runs and provides a deletion manifest daily. here's an example manifest showing items purged with job ids and hashes.
00:16:05 Tom: hashes of deleted items are kept  is that reversible?
00:16:20 Liam: hashes are one-way by default; we also can provide deletion receipts containing the hash that proves the item existed and was removed  auditors like that.
00:16:55 Priya: what's the difference if we pick Dedicated vs Hosted for this use case?
00:17:10 Maya: Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools and optional private network endpoints; it reduces blast radius and gives stronger data isolation, plus more granular control over retention windows and HSM keying. Hosted has quicker onboarding but we handle the control plane; for tight PCI/SOC2 your security team often prefers Dedicated or Private.
00:17:45 Sara: private on-prem  would that mean we host control plane?
00:17:55 Liam: Private gives you the option to run the control plane inside your VPC or on-prem appliance; you manage keys and network, and we provide the software + support. that's the strongest for data residency and auditable deletion requirements.
00:18:30 Tom: any gotchas around model caching holding onto PII in KV caches?
00:18:45 Liam: good callout  the runtime keeps short-term KV cache for performance, typically seconds to a few minutes. we scrub KV cache asynchronously if redaction is enabled, and in Dedicated/Private we can configure cache eviction policies or disable caching for specific routes.
00:19:15 Sara: how about logs produced by the model during generation - do you capture completions?
00:19:30 Liam: completions are treated as request outputs and subject to same storage controls. you can choose to strip completion text from logs or store only token counts and latencies.
00:19:55 [customer asks about demoing 'Optimize' suggestions]
00:20:10 Maya: yes, our Optimize toolkit runs a lightweight analysis of requests and suggests fields to redact and caching/batching profiles to reduce cost. it also flags potential privacy leaks. we'll show a sample analysis report.
00:20:40 Liam: opening Optimize -> Data Insights -> sample report. it lists top-k fields by entropy and suggests json-path rules; you can accept and deploy rules from that UI.
00:21:15 Priya: can we version redaction rules and roll back?
00:21:25 Liam: yes, rules are versioned and you can do canary rollouts per route. changes are audited.
00:21:55 Tom: compliance question: do you provide signed attestations for deletions for auditors?
00:22:05 Maya: we provide deletion receipts and audit bundles; for enterprise we can provide additional attestation language as part of contract. we'll include sample attestation text.
00:22:40 Sara: are there limits for how many redaction rules or performance impact?
00:22:55 Liam: rule evaluation is lightweight; we compile regexes and json-paths  at scale some complex rules can add CPU overhead but we offer pre-compiled rule profiles and suggest moving heavy patterns to edge pre-processing.
00:23:25 [short pause]
00:23:40 Priya: what about data residency across regions? if we have EU customers, can requests be stored only in eu-west-1?
00:23:55 Liam: yes, we support region pinning for storage and region-aware routing. Private deployments give you full control. Hosted offers region options but data persistence region is selectable per project.
00:24:30 Tom: do you have SSO/SAML integration for audit tracking of who changed rules?
00:24:40 Maya: yes, SSO + RBAC + admin approvals. changes to data controls can be set to require multi-admin approval.
00:25:05 Sara: any PCI-specific certification notes?
00:25:15 Liam: we're not a PCI processor ourselves  we're a platform. our guidance: keep card-present data out of request bodies where possible, use tokenization, and for stored items use customer-managed keys in a Dedicated/Private deployment. we'll share best-practice docs.
00:25:40 [Priya asks for demo of API deletion flow]
00:25:55 Liam: running a quick curl demo: POST /v1/requests/delete {scope: route: 'payments', before: '2026-12-01T00:00:00Z'} returns job_id: 5842; poll /jobs/5842 -> status: complete -> get /audit/jobs/5842/receipt returns signed receipt.
00:26:40 Tom: great. can that be integrated into our ticketing as webhook?
00:26:50 Maya: yes we support webhooks on job completion and SIEM export.
00:27:10 [customer requests SLA language around deletion timeframes]
00:27:25 Maya: we'll include proposed SLA language for deletion within contract; typical is 'deletion job processed within 24 hours, manifest available within 48 hours' for Hosted; Dedicated/Private can be tightened.
00:27:50 Sara: okay, cost question - does disabling request storage reduce costs?
00:27:58 Liam: yes materially. storage and egress are biggest drivers. also Optimize can suggest quantization and batching to reduce inference cost. we'll share cost delta examples.
00:28:30 Priya: anything else to show?
00:28:40 Liam: i want to show audit export quick example  navigating to Audit -> Exports -> generate signed bundle -> download link (sanitized example provided). also show logs view with redaction applied so you can see masked values inline.
00:29:20 Sara: looks good. one more question  who owns the deletion job logs? if hosted, are they accessible to redwood support?
00:29:40 Maya: support access is controlled by RBAC and request; for Hosted support can assist but access is logged and requires approval; for Dedicated/Private, you can restrict support access entirely or via a support token during onboarding.
00:30:05 Tom: we'll want to run an encryption review, so please include KMS key rotation docs and support for key import.
00:30:20 Maya: will do.
00:30:35 [wrap-up questions]
00:31:00 Priya: timeline recap: pilot -> security review -> procurement.
00:31:15 Maya: next steps: i'll send security docs + pricing, liam will spin up the test endpoint, and tom you'll confirm PII fields.
00:31:35 Sara: ok sounds good. any blocker for pilot?
00:31:45 Liam: just approval to run sample traffic; we can use synthetic data otherwise.
00:32:05 Maya: last thing  we'll include a sample audit bundle and a sanitized deletion receipt in the follow-up email.
00:32:20 [meeting ends, small chatter]
